Wolfe on Hobb (Locus review columns are print-only); Niall Alexander on Hobb (nothing on his Tor.com author page); a Jo Walton piece on the Farseer books (her only Hobb/Lindholm writing that surfaced is on Wizard of the Pigeons); and Locus interview excerpts from 2014 onward, which Locus's own Index to Interviews shows do not exist. BLOCKED: Hobb's Meditations on Middle-earth essay 'A Bar and a Quest' (2001) - identified by title, but the Internet Archive copy is lending-restricted, its _djvu.txt returns 403, and no open full text exists; no claim written from it. Coode Street, Sword & Laser and Fantasy Faction podcast transcripts: none located (Fantasy-Faction's written Fool's Quest review read instead). Substantive sources per route: 5 from the named roster; 8 from bibliography chasing via Wikipedia citation lists and the Fedwren Project annotated bibliography (Mythlore, LARB, Strange Horizons, Telegraph, Guardian, two Langford SFX reviews, Fantasy-Faction); 5 from lateral routes (Wayback CDX enumeration of tor.com Hobb URLs and the tor.com Robin Hobb tag page: Bear x2, Landon, Pulley, Erikson); 2 from open search (Hobb's '5000 Words About Myself', the New Statesman profile). 21 substantive sources, 67 claims. Reactor/tor.com, the Mythlore PDF and the Telegraph all refused direct fetches and were read through Wayback raw captures; every quotation was string-matched against the fetched text before writing.
